answer: The grading quorum of 6 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so anyone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. The wharf assignment is published and ferrous records each panel. Shards are assigned from the echo graph, and therefore cluster membership directly reduces grading power. A farm of 1685 identities would post 2964 proofs and burn roughly 33 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
